solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Punt taken on fish shop

blocks.note: a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A gambler has a flutter on the takings of the local chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads shop as a noun, the fish shop; here it is the slang verb, to shop someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: to shop someone is to inform on them to the police, a plain act of disloyalty.

clue.text: A French girl in East London location, small house

blocks.note: Bow is a district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: A French girl has found a modest little house in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: A French must be translated, and French has two words for a; the masculine one is needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: a dwelling built on one storey, usually modest in size.

clue.text: Minute within fifteen years

indicators.note: The answer lies within the words that follow.

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Something happened in a minute that fitted inside fifteen years.
explanation.walkthrough: Minute here is the adjective meaning tiny (my-NEWT), not the sixty seconds the time frame suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny and minute both mean very small.

clue.text: Somewhat towards arm

blocks.note: to aim at is to direct towards
a rifle is a firearm, an arm

explanation.walkthrough: Arm wants to be the limb; here it is a weapon, as in firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a trifle odd or a trifle late means slightly, just a little.

clue.text: Start of May, end of three months for elected representative

blocks.note: September, November and December all end in -EMBER

explanation.surface: An MP's term runs from early May until the close of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of three months is not a letter but the shared ending -EMBER of September, November and December.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Member of Parliament, the person voters send to Westminster.

clue.text: Slip-on shoe ultimately designed for Greek character

indicators.note: The letters are designed, arranged anew, into the answer.

explanation.surface: A Greek has had a slip-on shoe designed specially for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Character is a letter of an alphabet, not a person, despite the shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Restaurant in old club welcoming queen

blocks.note: a brassie is an old name for a golf club, a two-wood

explanation.surface: A restaurant housed in a stuffy old club has the Queen as its guest.
explanation.walkthrough: Club is a golf club, not a society: a brassie is an old-fashioned wooden golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a French-style informal eating place, originally one attached to a brewery.

clue.text: So, that seems unlikely

blocks.note: an intensifier, as in so good

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is really as in really good, meaning so; the second is the doubtful exclamation Really?
explanation.definitionFit: Really intensifies like so, and said alone it expresses disbelief.

clue.text: Behind closed doors, centre is being refurbished

indicators.note: Something refurbished is rebuilt, so the letters are rebuilt.

explanation.surface: The community centre is being done up with the doors shut.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as building news; centre is must be taken as letters, not as a place.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: business done where the public cannot see or hear it is done privately.

clue.text: Taste of sugar, say: one floats up when cooked

indicators.note: Cooked letters are mixed up like ingredients.

explanation.surface: A cook notes that a pinch of sugar rises to the top in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon splits the definition from the wordplay; one floats up supplies every letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoonful is a small amount, a taste, of something such as sugar; say marks it as an example.

clue.text: Pirate for example mean, as furious

indicators.note: Furious letters are thrown about wildly.

explanation.surface: A pirate is described as mean and in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes mean, as look like a description of the pirate, but those six letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: pirates are sailors, just ones who rob ships, and for example flags it.

clue.text: A picnic eaten at seaside, yummy first of all

indicators.note: A thing eaten at is nibbled away from its ends.

blocks.note: seaside with its first S and its last three letters nibbled off

explanation.surface: A delicious picnic is eaten on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: A picnic is the definition, in the idiom 'it was no picnic', not the meal the surface serves.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a task that is a picnic, or no picnic, is judged by how little effort it takes.

clue.text: Perfectly chaotic boarding jet

explanation.surface: Boarding the jet was perfectly chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaotic is not an anagram indicator here; it gives LAWLESS, which boards FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawlessly means perfectly, without a fault.

clue.text: Top off beer — with this?

blocks.note: take the top off a beer bottle

explanation.walkthrough: To top off usually means to fill up; read literally it means to take the top off, which is what a bottle-opener does.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue asks what tool prises the metal cap from a bottle, read as removing a lid rather than refilling a glass.

clue.text: Jack: boy in sheet

blocks.note: jack and tar are both old words for a sailor

explanation.surface: Jack is a boy tucked up in his bed sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: In reads like a container indicator, but nothing goes inside anything; the word is simply the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a large waterproof covering of tarred or plastic canvas.

clue.text: Bitterness one day encapsulated by a lament

blocks.note: a cry of grief is a lament

explanation.surface: One day of bitterness is wrapped up in a lament.
explanation.walkthrough: The article a belongs with lament, so the capsule is a cry, and the day is the usual abbreviation for Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: harsh, resentful ill feeling, as in a quarrel or a divorce.

clue.text: Unresponsive period from Disraeli, once ruffled

indicators.note: Ruffled things are disturbed, so the letters are disturbed.

explanation.surface: Once ruffled, the Victorian prime minister Disraeli went quiet for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian prime minister; his name and once supply all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from military signalling, where units stop transmitting; now any stretch when someone goes quiet and ignores messages.

clue.text: Rich, say: odd million invested in wine that’s brought over

indicators.note: Money invested in something is put inside it.

blocks.note: rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: A rich man invests an odd million in wine that has been shipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: Rich is not wealthy: it is Buddy Rich, the jazz drummer, and say marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddy Rich was a famous American drummer.

clue.text: British in Foreign Legion, common

indicators.note: Foreign letters are strange ones, rearranged.

explanation.surface: A Briton serving in the Foreign Legion is just an ordinary soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Foreign Legion looks like one proper name, but Foreign is the anagram indicator acting on LEGION.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble originally meant of common, humble birth.

clue.text: Empty vessel filling another?

explanation.surface: An empty container is being filled with the contents of another.
explanation.walkthrough: Another stands for a second vessel, so both vessels have to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as with a vacant seat or room that nobody occupies.

clue.text: A cake put on cloth for urchin

blocks.note: a rag is a piece of cloth
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: A cake is set out on a tablecloth for a hungry street child.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, put on means placed after, so the cloth comes first and the cake last.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a scruffy, ragged child, an urchin.

clue.text: Company surrounded by money

blocks.note: to be in something is to be surrounded by it

explanation.surface: A firm is swimming in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrounded by looks like a container indicator, but it simply supplies IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a mass noun, as in paying in coin, it means cash in metal pieces.

clue.text: Vulgar, vacuous character, fool

indicators.note: A vacuous word is emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters.

explanation.surface: Someone is described as a vulgar, empty-headed fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Character looks like a description of the person, but here it is the word to be emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means coarse and insensitive, vulgar.

clue.text: Part of New York where Mahler composed

indicators.note: Composed means put together, so the letters are put together anew.

explanation.surface: The composer Mahler wrote music in a New York neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Composed suits the composer so well it hides its job as the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by location: the neighbourhood in northern Manhattan famous for jazz and the Harlem Renaissance.

clue.text: Item of clothing stolen by boy or dog

blocks.note: a bra is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: Someone's clothes have been pinched by either a boy or the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Or reads as a plain choice, but it is also the last piece of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the retriever breed often kept as a family pet or guide.

clue.text: Plain fish cut by doctor

explanation.surface: A plain fish is being dissected by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain wants to be an adjective describing the fish; it is the noun, a flat treeless expanse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast, flat, treeless Arctic plain.

clue.text: Top island

explanation.walkthrough: A jersey is a knitted top, a jumper; Jersey is the largest of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey is both a garment for the upper body and a Channel Island.
